issues.detail: The two examples are prose descriptions of steps rather than runnable demonstrations with concrete inputs and outputs, so they are less realistic than the code in the Instructions section.

scenarios.name: filtered-search-fewer-rows-fix
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric element cleanly: post-filtering, `SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan` inside a transaction, B-tree/partial/partition alternatives and `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`. A covers the same ground but uses plain `SET` in its main example (only mentioning `SET LOCAL` afterward), gives shaky workarounds (`enable_indexscan`, a materialized CTE), and omits BUFFERS in its EXPLAIN suggestion.

scenarios.name: index-3072-dim-embeddings
scenarios.rationale: Both state the 2,000-dimension limit and give the halfvec cast expression index with halfvec_cosine_ops, and both stress that queries must use the same cast with ORDER BY <=> and LIMIT; A adds extra options (dimension reduction, binary quantization) and a version note, while B has a slightly less explicit limit statement for the cast but includes practical notes like iterative scan and CONCURRENTLY, so the two are near equal with A slightly more complete.

scenarios.name: node-semantic-search-with-pgvector-pg
scenarios.rationale: A registers pgvector types, uses toSql with parameterized args, wraps SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan in BEGIN/COMMIT, computes 1-distance, and leaves cutoff to app code; B skips pgvector registration and the transaction, only mentions SET as a note, and does not address app-side cutoff.
